evidence_set: Two New York State school panels: 5,468 public high-school students linked between fall 1971 and spring 1972 (5–6 months) and 985 graduated seniors re-contacted 5–9 months after graduation (winter 1972–1973). Linkage by self-generated codes matched 66% of fall students in the spring (60% of seniors); unmatched students included more people who used drugs. Each wave was weighted for the selection probabilities of schools and homerooms and for school response rates; the only correction described for unmatched cases is a weighting of the panel to reproduce first-wave marihuana use in the full cross-sectional sample.
